definition: means medical treatment for an illness / disease / injury which in the normal course would require care and treatment at a hospital but is actually taken while confined at home under any of the following circumstances: a. The condition of the patient is such that he / she is not in a condition to be removed to a hospital, or b. The patient takes treatment at home on account of non-availability of room in a hospital.
plain: Treatment taken at home that would normally have required a hospital bed, either because the patient could not be moved or because no bed was available.
whyItMatters: It is a genuine benefit that most people never learn they have. It usually requires the treatment to run beyond three days and to be certified as hospital-grade care, so it does not cover ordinary illness at home — but for elderly patients who cannot safely be moved, it is the clause that turns a refused claim into a paid one.
